historical_references.context: Ravan is mentioned as a Persian king who ruled over Al-Hind (India) during the early Islamic period. He is identified as Raja Dahapala or Dahapuraka in Indian texts. Ibn Kathir describes him as a powerful ruler who was a patron of learning and the sciences, particularly astronomy and astrology.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Biruni, The Chronology of Ancient Nations, p. 175-176 (1030 CE). The name Ravan carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Biruni identifies Ravan as a legendary king of India mentioned in Hindu mythology. He is described as a king of Lanka who abducted Sita, the wife of Rama, and held her captive in Ashoka Gardens. Ravan is depicted as a powerful sorcerer and a devotee of the god Shiva.
